title: Strong Acid - Strong Base Titration (HCl + NaOH)
indicator_color_transition: Colorless in acid, permanent faint faint pink at equivalence point (pH 8.2-10.0)
procedure_steps: Rinse burette with small volume of standard NaOH solution before filling.
Ensure burette tip is filled with solution and has no trapped air bubbles.
Pipette exactly 20.00 mL or 25.00 mL of unknown HCl into an Erlenmeyer flask.
Add 2 to 3 drops of phenolphthalein indicator. Swirl flask.
Record initial burette volume reading at eye level at the bottom of the meniscus.
Titrate while swirling continuously until a single drop causes a persistent faint pink color lasting 30 seconds.
guidance_speech: For HCl and NaOH titration, use phenolphthalein. The endpoint is reached when a single drop turns the colorless solution to a faint, persistent pink. If it turns dark magenta, you have overshot the endpoint.

title: Indicator Selection and Endpoints

data.name: Phenolphthalein
data.suitability: Strong Acid - Strong Base, Weak Acid - Strong Base

data.name: Bromothymol Blue
data.suitability: Strong Acid - Strong Base neutral point

guidance_speech: Phenolphthalein is ideal for strong acid with strong base titrations because the pH jump spans pH four to ten. Look for the very first permanent pale pink coloration.

title: Burette Meniscus Technique
guidance_speech: Position your eye level horizontally with the liquid level in the burette. Read the exact graduation at the bottom of the concave meniscus to within plus or minus 0.02 milliliters.

title: Overshot Endpoint Troubleshooting
guidance_speech: A dark magenta color means the titration endpoint was overshot by excess base. You must discard this run and repeat, adding titrant drop by drop near the expected volume.

title: Molarity and Neutralization Stoichiometry
formula: C_acid * V_acid = C_base * V_base (for 1:1 monoprotic stoichiometry)
guidance_speech: Use the neutralization equivalence formula: C acid times V acid equals C base times V base. For diprotic acids like sulfuric acid, remember each mole of acid delivers two moles of protons.
